sectors.name: Technology
themes: Indonesia's tech sector is decoupling from US weakness, driven by domestic digital adoption and government-backed infrastructure spending, making local tech names structurally resilient.
AI-driven storage and compute demand (AMD, STX, SNDK) remains a durable multi-year cycle, with memory and HBM supply constraints favoring pricing power.
Optical and connectivity plays (LITE, GLW) face margin pressure from US rate volatility, but long-term AI data-center buildouts keep their growth trajectory intact.
sectors.ai: Buy SLIS and NBIS on momentum, but rotate into AMD and STX for sustained AI/storage demand; trim US-exposed names like GLW and LITE given the -0.38% US drag. Indonesia's +0.60% tech outperformance signals local liquidity tailwinds, so overweight ID-listed tech proxies while hedging US semis volatility.

sectors.name: Financials
themes: Indonesia financials are outperforming US peers on domestic rate-cut expectations, which lower funding costs and boost credit demand, a durable driver for banks and multifinance firms.
Small-cap financials like STAR, XCIS, and TUGU are seeing outsized gains on retail liquidity and index rebalancing flows, a structural trend as local investors favor high-beta names.
Regulatory tailwinds in digital banking and insurance, exemplified by AHAP and ASMI, support long-term earnings diversification beyond traditional lending, underpinning sector resilience.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in Indonesia financials, led by STAR and XCIS, as domestic liquidity and rate-cut expectations drive outperformance vs US peers. Favor AHAP and ASMI for continued upside, but trim PEGE after its run. Maintain neutral aggregate exposure, rotate from US financials into ID names on relative strength.

sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Indonesia's thermal coal exports remain structurally supported by Asian demand and high-calorie premium pricing, sustaining margins for large-cap producers like BYAN and ADMR.
Nickel and tin downstreaming policies, including smelter mandates and export bans, continue to reprice domestic miners like TINS and ALKA toward value-added processing.
Energy transition capex in Indonesia, from geothermal to coal-to-ammonia projects, is creating a multi-year rerating catalyst for integrated players with cash flow to diversify.
sectors.ai: Buy selective thermal coal and nickel names on the IDX rotation, as BYAN and ADMR lead with volume-backed gains while ENRG's spike is speculative. Favor ADMR for coking coal exposure and TINS for tin upside, but trim into strength given WATCH signal—position sizing matters more than chasing momentum.

sectors.ai: Buy VKTR and NRG on strength; both are scaling EV and geothermal exposure with clear catalysts. Trim ARKO if it extends gains without volume confirmation. sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Rural consumption and digital penetration are structurally lifting demand for FMCG products, benefiting companies with strong distribution networks in tier-2/3 cities.
Premiumization and health-consciousness are durable drivers, pushing growth toward higher-margin functional foods and personal care items.
Election-cycle fiscal transfers and social aid programs are expected to sustain purchasing power, underpinning volume growth for mass-market consumer staples.
sectors.ai: Buy dips in Indonesia consumer names with direct rural distribution and digital-led demand, as the sector's modest aggregate masks strong single-stock momentum. Prioritize AGAR, UDNG, and SONA for near-term alpha, but rotate into defensive staples like GUNA and HADE for stability. Watch for policy-driven consumption catalysts ahead of elections.

sectors.name: Healthcare
themes: Indonesia's healthcare demand is structurally driven by a young, expanding middle class and rising chronic disease prevalence, insulating domestic players from global rate cycles.

Government push for universal health coverage (JKN) and local manufacturing incentives (e.g., import substitution for medical devices) creates durable tailwinds for domestic producers and distributors
US healthcare names (CVS, CNC) face margin compression from pharmacy benefit manager reforms and Medicaid redeterminations, making them structurally less attractive than ID-focused operators.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian healthcare names with domestic revenue exposure, as the sector's +0.34% ID outperformance versus US -0.27% confirms local resilience. SRAJ (+15.38%) and PEHA (+13.64%) signal momentum in pharma distribution and hospital supplies; add on pullbacks, but avoid US-linked laggards. Position for Q3 earnings catalysts, prioritizing firms with pricing power and government procurement ties.

sectors.name: Logistics
themes: Indonesia's e-commerce penetration remains sub-20%, driving structural demand for last-mile and cold-chain logistics providers like ASSA and BN4 well beyond 2026.
Government push for downstream processing and new capital (IKN) is accelerating inter-island freight and port infrastructure investment, benefiting GIAA and SHIP as volume multipliers.
Regional supply-chain reshoring from China to ASEAN is lifting warehousing and third-party logistics margins, with AMKBY and CBRE capturing premium industrial real estate demand.
sectors.ai: Buy logistics exposure into strength: AMKBY (+8.4%) and TAXI (+7.1%) confirm foreign capital rotation into Indonesian supply-chain names, while GIAA's +5.6% signals cargo-rate tailwinds. Add on pullbacks to BN4 and ASSA for domestic e-commerce volume leverage; trim SHIP if it breaks below support.

sectors.name: Crypto & Digital Assets
themes: Tokenized real-world assets (RWA) are gaining durable institutional traction as on-chain treasury and credit products scale, making ONDO a structural compounder.
AI-agent and identity-verification tokens (WLD, HYPE) are becoming the primary retail narrative for 2025, with recurring usage rather than one-off speculation.
Privacy and proof-of-work assets (ZEC) face episodic regulatory catalysts but lack sustained demand, limiting their role to tactical trades only.
sectors.ai: Buy selective beta into tokenized-RWA and AI-agent narratives (ONDO, WLD, HYPE) on strength, but keep size modest; BTW's +19.9% is a low-liquidity spike, not a trend. Rotate out of pure meme names (PUMP) into cash-flowing protocols. Watch for a BTC-led pullback to add; avoid chasing ZEC's regulatory-driven bounce.
